claims.text: Established LLMs align with human estimates from the Fagen–Ulmschneider survey only for some words of estimative probability presented in English.
Divergence between human and LLM interpretation of words of estimative probability is observed for prompts using gendered contexts.
Divergence between human and LLM interpretation of words of estimative probability is observed for prompts using Chinese contexts.
GPT-4 exhibits performance gaps when consistently mapping statistical expressions of uncertainty to appropriate words of estimative probability.

evidence.description: Empirical study comparing LLM responses to human estimates from the Fagen–Ulmschneider survey shows alignment only for a subset of English WEPs.
Empirical evaluation demonstrated divergences in WEP interpretation when prompts contained gendered contexts.
Empirical evaluation demonstrated divergences in WEP interpretation when prompts contained Chinese contexts.
Investigation into GPT-4's mapping of statistical uncertainty expressions to WEPs revealed significant performance gaps.

methodologies.name: Empirical WEP Alignment Evaluation
methodologies.description: An empirical study comparing human survey estimates with LLM interpretations of words of estimative probability across varied context conditions.

limitations.text: Established LLMs align with human estimates only for some WEPs presented in English, failing to align consistently across all WEPs.
LLM interpretation of WEPs diverges from human norms when presented in gendered or Chinese contexts.
GPT-4 displays significant performance gaps in consistently mapping statistical expressions of uncertainty to appropriate WEPs.
